action.reasoning: The toolbar Zoom dropdown is the standard way to set zoom; open it to reveal 150%.
action.expectation: the zoom dropdown opens listing percentage options including 150%

lesson.preamble: Zoom feels like it should change the document, but it changes nothing about it. The page is still the same size, the text still prints the same, and anyone else opening this file sees whatever they had set. Zoom is a property of your eyes and your screen, not of the page — which is why it lives in the toolbar with the view controls rather than anywhere near formatting.
lesson.generalization: Font size changes the document; zoom changes the window you're looking at it through. Whenever a control makes things bigger, it's worth asking which of those two it's doing — one travels with the file to everyone who opens it, the other stays with you and is forgotten the moment you close the tab.

steps.intent: This box shows the current magnification of the page — it almost certainly reads 100% right now. It's a dropdown, and opening it gives you the set of magnifications Docs offers, rather than making you type one.
hints: You're not changing the text, you're changing how close you are to it. Look for the control that's already reporting a percentage.
In the toolbar, just right of the print and spelling icons, showing '100%'.

wrongHints.Font size: That makes the letters themselves bigger — bigger on screen, bigger on paper, bigger for everyone who opens the file. Zoom leaves the document untouched and only moves you closer to it.
wrongHints.Styles: Styles describe what a line of text is — a heading, a title, body text. Nothing about the document's meaning is changing here, only your view of it.
wrongHints.Print: Reasonable, since print has its own scaling — but that scaling applies to paper. You want the page bigger on screen, which is a separate setting.

steps.intent: Pick 150%. You're telling Docs to draw the page half again as large as life. The list is a set of fixed steps rather than a slider, because these are the magnifications that keep text crisp.
hints: Half again as big as the 100% you started at — find that value in the list of percentages.
In the open dropdown, two below 100%, between 125% and 200%.

wrongHints.Fit: Fit sizes the page to whatever your window happens to be, so the number changes every time you resize. You want a fixed 150%, not a moving target.
wrongHints.200%: That's double, not half again. The difference matters if you're matching a specific magnification rather than just making things larger.
wrongHints.100%: That's the size you're already at — the page drawn at its true dimensions. 150% is the one that enlarges it.
